newsitem.title: USA: Continental sees no change in Boeing order.
newsitem.headline: Continental sees no change in Boeing order.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc said Wednesday it does not expect to alter its plans to buy aircraft exclusively from Boeing Co over the next 20 years, despite the Seattle-based aircraft manufacturer's agreement not to enforce the exclusive contract.

In an effort to appease the European Commission's concerns about its planned merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp, Boeing agreed not to enforce the exclusive-provider contracts it forged with three U.S. airlines. Boeing also made other concessions.

"Nothing we've done has unraveled," said Continental chairman Gordon Bethune. "The fact that we have the opportunity to date other partners ... dosen't mean we're going to do it. We kind of like our partner."

"We have a deal with the Boeing company and we expect Boeing to live up to it. What Boeing has said publicly is that they would not enforce our unwillingness to live up to our deal. But Continental lives up to its deals and we don't have to be enforced to do it," Bethune said.
Continental said it would not make economic sense to purchase planes from another manufacturer, since adding different jets would increase costs for additional parts, training and equipment.
Continental also said its 20-year commitment to Boeing makes sense since aircraft typically have a 20-25 year lifespan.
